# Comms Quick Reference
A compact reference for radio controls, ranges, settings, and common effects.
For full instructions, see [textlink="AN/PRC-117G Radio" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] and [textlink="Field Headsets" link="AU14CommsHeadsets"].

## AN/PRC operator training
The AN/PRC control panel can be used by:
- [bold]GOVFOR and OPFOR[/bold] - Commanding Officer, Adjutant, staff officers, engineering officers, intelligence officers, synthetics, Squad Leaders, Fireteam Leaders, and Radio Traffic Operators - [bold]CLF[/bold] - Cell Leader and Radio Operator - anyone who has read a [bold]field radio operator's pamphlet[/bold]
The handset can be used without radio-operator training.

### Combat-net relays
Combat nets require relay coverage from at least one compatible source:
- powered AN/PRC worn by a trained operator - deployed retransmission station - command-post antenna mast - powered communications array - vehicle radio - powered field antenna mast keyed to your faction - CLF clandestine base station or relay set - mast or array carrying a CLF feeder tap
Colony and civilian channels are not relay-gated.
## Net splicing
A CLF Radio Operator can use a [bold]net splice kit[/bold] to add CLF nets to compatible communications infrastructure.
Splicing does not remove or interfere with the host's existing nets.

### Splice rules
- PROBE reads zero when the nearest carrier is more than 30 positions away - LOCK succeeds within 4 positions of a carrier - each probe adds 1.5% detection - a failed lock adds 30% detection and consumes 2 probes - using all probes or filling the detection meter fails the attempt - a failed junction remains faulted for 90 seconds - junctions spark while being worked and while faulted - an installed tap can be removed in eight seconds - removing a tap returns a CLF fill card - opening a spliced field mast's feed knocks the tap off and drops its CLF fill card

[bold]Mode[/bold]
[bold]Function[/bold]
[bold]Benefits[/bold]
[bold]Limitations[/bold]
[bold]FH[/bold]
Frequency hopping
Reduces jamming by one tier.
1.5x battery use and a small DF signature.
[bold]SC[/bold]
Single-channel secured traffic
0.75x battery use and no DF signature while secured.

[bold]CT[/bold]

Hidden without the matching fill; no DF signature.

Plain-text traffic
0.5x battery use.
Unencrypted, increases jamming by one tier, and produces the largest DF signature.
A matching COMSEC fill secures FH, SC, and CT traffic.
PT is always transmitted in the clear.

## Squelch
Squelch filters degraded and noisy traffic. It does not improve signal quality.
[bold]SQL[/bold]
[bold]Filtering[/bold]
[bold]0[/bold]
Passes all traffic, including heavy static.
[bold]1[/bold]
Suppresses heavy static and undecodable encrypted traffic.
[bold]2[/bold]
Suppresses medium jammer degradation.
[bold]3[/bold]
Default. Suppresses light jamming and heavily degraded fringe traffic.
[bold]4[/bold]
Maximum filtering. Can suppress lightly degraded long-range traffic.
Lower squelch allows more degraded traffic through.
Higher squelch produces a quieter receiver but can hide weak stations.
## COMSEC
[bold]Action[/bold]
[bold]Result[/bold]
Insert fill card
Secures compatible faction traffic in FH, SC, and CT.
[bold]ZEROIZE[/bold]
Ejects the loaded fill card.
[bold]DESTROY[/bold]
Destroys the loaded fill card.
[bold]RECRYPTO[/bold]
Invalidates all older faction fill cards. Requires Commanding Officer, Adjutant, or Advisor authority.
Captured current fill
Allows compatible secured traffic from that faction to be decoded until they recrypto.
Replacement fill cards are available through supply.
## Direction finding
Direction-finding signatures, from highest to lowest risk:
- PT traffic - faction-net traffic without a matching fill - secured FH traffic
Secured SC and CT traffic produce no DF signature.
Repeated detectable transmissions from the same location increase detection chance.
DF risk begins decreasing after roughly one minute without another qualifying transmission.
[bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] reports which stations receive the current net and whether reception is clear or degraded.
Inside a jammer field, RADIO CHECK also provides a bearing toward the strongest jammer.
## Search receiver
[bold]START SEARCH[/bold] sweeps for other factions' radio traffic.
While searching:
[bold]Effect[/bold]
[bold]Value[/bold]
Loaded nets
Disconnected while searching.
Transmission
Disabled.
Full-band sweep
About 20 seconds.
Detection window
Signal transmitted within 20 seconds, on the same level, and within 120 tiles at MED, 72 at LO, or 180 at HI.
Resolution
Around 3 lines at one transmission per minute; busy nets can resolve in about 1 minute.
Partial-contact decay
Begins after 2 minutes without traffic.
Contacts reveal additional frequency digits as more transmissions are detected.
Once a net is resolved:
[bold]Result[/bold]
[bold]Effect[/bold]
Bearing
Compass bearing and distance rounded to 10 tiles, at most once every 10 seconds per net. Secured SC and CT do not provide bearings.
Tactical map
Marks the transmitter for 8 seconds for your faction.
Key trial
One per encrypted line, up to 12 stored. Enemy keys contain 6 unique symbols from A-H.
A broken key allows that radio to read the faction's encrypted traffic until they perform a recrypto.
## Net log
The AN/PRC stores the last [bold]50[/bold] radio entries.
Enemy traffic is marked [bold]INTERCEPT[/bold].
- [bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] - print all stored traffic - [bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] - print only intercepted traffic

## AUTO configuration
The guided panel normally uses [bold]AUTO[/bold]:
- FH waveform - MED output - squelch 3 - wearer's callsign
[bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold] on the SETTINGS tab restores these settings and clears manual faceplate configuration changes.
